extraction.name: EgoLife Dataset
extraction.description: A comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset with intensive annotation. Six participants lived together for one week, continuously recording their daily activities—including discussions, shopping, cooking, socializing, and entertainment—using AI glasses for multimodal egocentric video capture, along with synchronized third-person-view video references. The dataset includes audio transcripts, visual-audio narrations, and QA annotations, and supports the EgoLifeQA benchmark for long-context, life-oriented question-answering tasks.
extraction.creator: The EgoLife Team (LMMs-Lab, NTU S-Lab, and collaborating institutions)
extraction.citeAs: The EgoLife Team. EgoLife: Towards Egocentric Life Assistant. arXiv:2503.03803v1 [cs.CV], 5 Mar 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Six volunteers lived together for seven days in a custom-designed environment called the EgoHouse. Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses and captured multimodal egocentric videos approximately 8 hours per day. Fifteen strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded third-person perspectives, and millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data. Recordings were structured into three-hour segments due to storage limitations. Primary investigators actively monitored participants and provided gentle prompts to encourage engagement in meaningful activities. Activities included discussions, shopping, cooking, socializing, music, dance, and an Earth Day party preparation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Passive Data Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Due to storage limitations, recordings are structured into three-hour segments. During data upload and storage clearance (approximately one hour every three hours), participants were instructed to remain in their rooms and limit activities to resting or non-essential tasks, resulting in gaps in the recorded footage.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Egocentric multimodal video from 6 Meta Aria glasses (video, audio, IMU, gaze); third-person video from 15 GoPro cameras (Beijing) and 6 cameras (Milan); millimeter-wave radar data from 2 TI IWR6843 (60GHz) mmWave monostatic radars with DCA1000 data capture boards (Beijing); WiFi channel state information (CSI) from 3 Asus RT-AX82U devices (Milan only).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Seven-day data collection period (Beijing session); one-day session in Milan (approximate dates: April 2024 based on activity diary references to April 16-17).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Videos were split into 5-minute clips and slowed to 0.8x speed for annotation. Initial narrations (361K brief phrases) were merged using GPT-4o-mini into 25K merged captions, then expanded into visual-audio captions by pairing with representative frames (sampled at 1 FPS) and corresponding transcripts, summarized by GPT-4o. Activity categorization was automatically performed using GPT-4o on visual-audio captions with timestamps. For EgoLifeQA, prompts for each question type were fed into GPT-4o in batches to generate approximately 100K timestamped QA candidates per participant, which were then filtered to 1K high-quality questions per participant and further refined to 500 QA per participant.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data processing pipeline (EgoSync) synchronized multi-source data (video, audio, IMU) from Aria glasses and GoPro cameras. Privacy protection was applied via EgoBlur (blurring faces, bystander faces, and vehicle license plates; muting sensitive audio segments; blurring sensitive screen content). Audio tracks from six participants were merged, speech recognition applied, and diarization used to differentiate speakers. Audio was then split into six individual tracks. Radar data was processed using the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection algorithm. WiFi CSI data was collected using the AX-CSI platform. Multimodal signal data was aligned with video data using timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcript annotations: merged audio tracks, applied speech recognition (Whisper), used open-source diarization to differentiate speakers, then human reviewers refined each participant's audio track. Caption annotations: annotators used video editing software (CapCut) to provide continuous narrations on 5-minute clips slowed to 0.8x speed, covering all actions, interactions, and environmental details; narrations were transcribed and reviewed. GPT-4o-mini merged phrases into captions; GPT-4o expanded them into visual-audio captions verified by human annotators. EgoLifeQA annotations: GPT-4o generated ~100K QA candidates per participant from visual-audio captions; annotators reviewed AI-generated questions as SRT files synced with video, filtered to questions requiring information from at least 5 minutes prior, refined to 500 high-quality QAs per participant, and generated multiple-choice distractors. Annotators also labeled whether audio was required and specified look-back time (certification length).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: CapCut (video editing software with dubbing functions) for caption narration; SRT file format for QA annotation review synced with video.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Initial AI-generated QA candidates (~100K per participant) were filtered to less than 1% (1K high-quality questions per participant) through rigorous selection, with preference for questions requiring longer dependencies and strong real-world relevance. Only questions requiring information from at least 5 minutes prior were retained. Human annotators further refined these to 500 final QAs per participant. Annotators also specified whether audio was required and the certification length (look-back time) for each question.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The EgoLife project is described as ongoing, with plans to expand the dataset to cover broader languages, locations, and activities. Data has been collected from two environments (Beijing and Milan); the Beijing dataset is fully annotated and released, while the Milan dataset will be detailed in upcoming EgoLife blog series. The project intends to continue annotation partnerships for future EgoLife versions.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset involves six participants whose daily activities, social interactions, conversations, and behaviors are recorded. Faces of participants and bystanders are blurred. Vehicle license plates are blurred. Sensitive audio segments are muted. Sensitive screen content (e.g., passwords, personal data) is blurred. Participant identities are used within the dataset for identity recognition tasks (RelationMap QA type). The dataset captures interpersonal dynamics, habits, health-related behaviors, and social interactions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: EgoButler and the EgoLifeQA dataset hold significant potential to enhance human-AI interaction, particularly in personalized assistance and context-aware applications. EgoButler could support daily activities, personal organization, and contextual reminders, improving quality of life especially for individuals needing consistent support, such as the elderly or those with cognitive challenges. In educational and professional settings, egocentric AI could facilitate learning, task tracking, and skill development. Privacy and ethical considerations must be addressed to ensure user autonomy and trust. The project aims to foster AI companions capable of supporting individuals in a socially and ethically responsible manner.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset was intentionally started with a narrow setting to build a strong foundation, sacrificing some generalizability (e.g., single language/scenario). The primary language is Chinese, limiting linguistic diversity. The dataset involves only six participants in a controlled shared living environment, which may not represent the full diversity of daily life activities, cultures, or demographics. The EgoLife week was structured around a specific goal (Earth Day party preparation), which may bias the activity distribution.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to six participants in a single shared living environment over one week. The primary language is Chinese (with one English-language subset from Milan). Recordings have gaps due to three-hour storage cycle constraints. The dataset currently covers a narrow range of languages, locations, and activities. EgoGPT's speech understanding is incomplete and struggles with laughter and emotions. Identity recognition tends to overfit to early observations (Day-1 fine-tuning). EgoRAG lacks multi-step reasoning and performs single-pass retrieval without iterative refinement.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and fine-tuning egocentric video-language models (EgoGPT trained on EgoIT-99K and EgoLife Day-1 data); benchmarking long-context egocentric video understanding (EgoLifeQA benchmark with EntityLog, EventRecall, HabitInsight, RelationMap, TaskMaster tasks); evaluation of multimodal egocentric AI assistants; research in long-duration activity understanding, interpersonal dynamics, identity recognition, habit analysis, and personalized AI assistance.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each 5-minute video clip receives continuous narration annotations. Each participant receives approximately 500 final QA annotations. Visual-audio captions are generated at clip level (25K merged captions total). Transcripts are annotated at the utterance level with speaker diarization.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Whisper (OpenAI speech recognition, Whisper Large v3) for transcript generation; open-source diarization algorithm (Whisper Diarization) for speaker differentiation; GPT-4o-mini for merging narration phrases into captions; GPT-4o for expanding merged captions into visual-audio captions and generating QA candidates; GPT-4o for activity categorization from visual-audio captions with timestamps; EgoBlur for face and sensitive content blurring.
